title: `elicitation/create` (URL)
description: A server request that sends the user out of band to a URL, for interactions such as sign-in that must not pass through the client.
question: Can the framework hand a user off to an external URL and resume?
why: Form mode is explicitly forbidden from collecting credentials, so URL mode is the sanctioned path for sign-in flows. A framework that implements only form mode leaves servers with no compliant way to authenticate a user mid-task.
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.

notes.crewai: CrewAI 1.15.26: `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` takes only server parameters, and mcpadapt opens its `ClientSession` with no callbacks, so the client declares no elicitation capability and the server's `elicitation/create` is refused (`Elicitation not supported`).
notes.genkit_js: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: `GenkitMcpClient` builds its SDK `Client` with only the `roots` capability and handler, so a URL-mode `elicitation/create` gets `Method not found` and there is no option to add a handler.
notes.openai-agents: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.23.1: `MCPServerStdio` forwards only `message_handler` to its `ClientSession`, which sees notifications, not requests. With no elicitation hook the client declares no elicitation capability and the server's `elicitation/create` is refused (`Elicitation not supported`).
notes.ms_agent_framework: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: The `ClientSession` that `MCPTool.connect` builds gets only `message_handler`, `logging_callback` and `sampling_callback`, and `MCPTool` has no parameter for this, so the SDK answers the server with an error.
notes.autogen: AutoGen 0.7.5: `McpWorkbench` opens its `ClientSession` with no elicitation callback and takes none, so the server's request is refused.
notes.vercel_ai: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): `onElicitationRequest` accepts only `ElicitationRequestSchema`, which requires `params.requestedSchema`. A URL-mode request carries none, so the client answers -32602 "Invalid elicitation request" before the registered handler sees it, even with `capabilities.elicitation.url` declared.
notes.openai_agents_js: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: the `MCPServerStdio` / `MCPServerStreamableHttp` options take no sampling, elicitation or roots handler, and the SDK registers none on the MCP client it builds, so the server's URL-mode `elicitation/create` request is answered with Method not found.
notes.semantic_kernel: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: `MCPPluginBase` opens its ClientSession with no `elicitation_callback` and takes none.
notes.llamaindex: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `BasicMCPClient` takes a `sampling_callback` and nothing for elicitation, so the client declares no elicitation capability and the server's URL-mode `elicitation/create` is refused (`Elicitation not supported`).
notes.pi: Pi (@earendil-works/pi-mcp 1.1.0): `McpClient` takes no elicitation handler and registers none, so an `elicitation/create` request is answered with Method not found. A caller could hand-register one with `setRequestHandler` and declare the capability through the `capabilities` option, which is protocol work rather than a client feature.
notes.google_adk_js: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `MCPSessionManager.createSession` builds `new Client({name: 'MCPClient', version: '1.0.0'})` with no capabilities and no request handlers, and `MCPToolset` takes no client hooks. URL-mode `elicitation/create` is refused (`Method not found`).
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` builds its fastmcp `Client` with no elicitation handler and exposes no hook to add one, so URL elicitation is refused.
notes.haystack: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPClient` builds its `ClientSession(read, write)` with no sampling, elicitation, roots or message callback, and neither the server info nor `MCPToolset` takes one, so the server's URL-mode `elicitation/create` got no answer and the tool call failed.
notes.smolagents: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): `smolagents.MCPClient` takes server parameters, `adapter_kwargs` and `structured_output` only, and mcpadapt opens its `ClientSession` with no callbacks, so the client declares no elicitation capability and the server's URL-mode `elicitation/create` is refused (`Elicitation not supported`).
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy takes no elicitation handler. The server's request is answered only by a `elicitation_callback` registered on the caller's own `mcp.Client`, which DSPy is handed by `Tool.from_mcp_tool` and never configures. DSPy itself offers no route.
notes.spring_ai: Spring AI 2.0.1: `@McpElicitation` handles form mode only. URL mode needs `spec.urlElicitation(...)` in an `McpClientCustomizer<McpClient.SyncSpec>` bean, which hands the request to the MCP SDK's builder unchanged, plus rebuilt capabilities declaring `elicitation.url`.
notes.beeai: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: no elicitation handler. URL elicitation works only on a `ClientSession` the caller builds and hands `MCPTool.from_client`, which BeeAI uses as given; the session BeeAI opens itself for a transport has no callbacks.
notes.crewai-native: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient.connect` builds its `ClientSession` from the transport streams alone, with no `elicitation_callback`, and `MCPServerStdio`/`MCPServerHTTP`/`MCPServerSSE` take no hook for it, so the client does not declare the capability and the server's request is refused.
notes.google_adk_java: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `McpSessionManager` builds the `McpSyncClient` with empty client capabilities and no elicitation handler, and neither `McpToolset` nor `McpTool` takes one, so `elicitation/create` is answered `Method not found`.
notes.langchain4j: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: `DefaultMcpClient` registers no elicitation handler at 2025-11-25 and never answers an `elicitation/create` request. The tool call waits until `toolExecutionTimeout` and fails with `There was a timeout executing the tool`.
notes.koog: Koog 1.3.0-beta: no Koog API. `Client.setElicitationHandler` on the Kotlin SDK `Client` before `fromClient` answers URL-mode `elicitation/create`.
notes.google_adk_go: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): mcptoolset has no elicitation option. A `mcp.ClientOptions.ElicitationHandler` with `Capabilities.Elicitation.URL` set on the `*mcp.Client` the caller passes as `mcptoolset.Config.Client` answers the server's request, so it works, but only by configuring go-sdk rather than the toolset.
